sections.h2: Recycled PET emits 59-79% less carbon than virgin PET per kilogram

chart.title: Recycled PET needs 1.4 kg CO2e per kg, against 3.4 kg for virgin PET
chart.sub: Carbon footprint of PET resin, kg CO2e per kg.
chart.source: Commonly cited lifecycle figures, as used in the post.

sections.means: Commonly cited figures put rPET at 1.4 kg CO2e per kg against 3.4 kg for virgin PET, a 59-79% reduction depending on the process comparison.
sections.todo: Keep recovered PET in closed-loop bottle recycling, since each reprocessed tonne avoids a tonne of virgin polymer.

sections.h2: India's PET recovery is high, and informal kabadiwalas do most of the collecting

chart.title: Industry and CPCB figures both put India's PET recovery at 92-95%
chart.sub: Share of PET bottles recovered, %. Both are reported figures, not audited.
chart.source: Industry figure; CPCB data as cited in the post.

sections.means: Both figures are directional, and the high rate rests on kabadiwalas who handle an estimated 90% of solid waste collection and sorting.
sections.todo: Bring kabadiwalas and informal waste pickers into the formal EPR system so their collection is named and credited.

sections.h2: Rigid-packaging recycled content must rise from 30% to 60% by FY2028-29

chart.title: Recycled-content targets rise in all three rigid-packaging categories
chart.sub: Target share of recycled content by FY2028-29, %.

sections.means: Category I rigid packaging rises from 30% to 60%, and PET in food-grade packaging moves from 30% to 40% from 1 April 2026.
sections.todo: Certify recycled-content proof for food-grade PET, since collection alone cannot show what goes into new packaging.
